title: Seo 2003: centroid distance of erector spinae at L3-L4 (F, supine)

imaging.plane: transverse cross-sectional image at L3/4 (orientation relative to disc not stated)

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm; AP distance between ellipse centres (long/short axis intersection) of muscle and vertebral body; mean of right and left

source.authors: Seo A, Lee JH, Kusaka Y
source.sample: 250 subjects (152 M, 98 F); healthy Japanese volunteers without back-pain treatment, age 15-75

how_to_simulate: Cut a transverse plane at the L3/L4 level.
Take the PCSA-weighted centroid of erector spinae (each side) in that plane and its AP offset from the vertebral body centre.
Average right and left and compare (+ anterior / - posterior). Centroid distance, not a moment arm.
protocol.notes: Paper does not say whether multifidus is included in "erector spinae" (size ~24 cm2/side in men suggests the whole paraspinal mass). Authors call it moment arm length. cm -> mm.

extraction.check_notes: Table 1 single-line rows, unambiguous in text; re-read all values.
